historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, a trough-to-normal span that skips the supercycle base); also ~3% TEU lifting growth FY2018-FY2025 (6.70m -> 7.87m TEU, 2.3%/yr) plus price
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (18.9%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (3.5%) and the 3yr series are all negative: book value was built by the FY2021-22 freight supercycle (US$17bn of NPAT) and has been flat since as payouts matched earnings. Neither the equity nor the 3yr CAGRs is a usable growth rate for a cyclical; the scenario paths are built bottom-up from volumes, rates and the newbuild programme instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs undefined: FY2025 owner FCF is negative (-35.1 reported, -691.2 after lease principal) because of newbuild instalments, and FY2023 was also negative. SBC is nil so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF coincide; interest income is already outside OCF.

scenario_narratives.base: Freight rates normalise from the Red Sea era. FY2026 revenue edges up ~3% on record liftings (H1 +6%) but H2 margins compress under the early peak season, oil-price spike and EU ETS costs. In 2027-28 the record global orderbook (~30% of the fleet) delivers just as Suez routings resume, releasing the ~10% of capacity the Cape diversion absorbed: revenue per TEU falls back toward ~US$1,000 and EBITDA (ex interest) troughs at 15%, roughly FY2023's level without its contract carry-over. OOIL is simultaneously paying ~US$1.5-1.7bn/yr of newbuild instalments, so owner FCF is negative for four years and is funded from the US$5.8bn cash pile. From 2030 the consolidated, alliance-disciplined industry earns a 19% IFRS-16 EBITDA mid-cycle margin (op margin ~7%), above the 2012-19 average but below 2023-25, and the fleet renewal cuts the charter bill as owned methanol/LNG tonnage replaces leased ships. Liftings grow ~3%/yr.
scenario_narratives.bull: Disruption persists and discipline holds. Red Sea transits stay largely closed through 2027 and US tariff/Section 301 rounds keep supply chains re-routing, so the trough is shallow (EBITDA 19-19.5%). Liner scrapping of the old Panamax/ post-Panamax fleet and slow-steaming for EU ETS/IMO carbon costs absorb much of the orderbook. OOCL's fuel-efficient dual-fuel fleet (one of the youngest in the industry by 2030) earns a cost advantage, the charter bill falls to 4.5% of revenue, and through-cycle EBITDA settles at 23% - the FY2023-H1 2026 average ex interest. COSCO keeps the 40-50% payout and the cash pile intact.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2016-style overcapacity cycle. The orderbook lands into a Red Sea reopening and weaker US imports after a new tariff round; rates fall below pre-COVID inflation-adjusted levels, revenue drops ~20% over 2027-28 and EBITDA ex interest falls to 10-11% (operating losses after leases and depreciation). OOIL still pays the US$5.4bn of contracted instalments, burning roughly half of its net cash, while the Seaspan charters and the LBCT minimum-lift commitment lock in fixed costs. Mid-cycle EBITDA recovers only to 15.5% (the IFRS-16-equivalent of FY2018-19). Governance risk sits here too: COSCO (~75%) directs capital to group priorities - more newbuilds - rather than minority returns.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a container liner on a through-cycle margin, never on the latest year: FY2021-22 supercycle profits are excluded, the 2023-26 Red Sea era is treated as above mid-cycle, and the newbuild programme already contracted is charged in full as capex. Net cash is credited at face after deducting the LBCT onerous provision and the declared dividend; interest on that cash is kept out of the flows so it is not counted twice.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is the dominant assumption: each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin (held from 2030) moves the base value by roughly US$1.3/share (~HK$10); the current price sits between the base (19%) and bull (23%, with a lighter charter bill) cases, much closer to bull - i.e. the market is capitalising Red Sea-era margins as normal.
Timing of the Red Sea reopening and orderbook deliveries sets the depth of the 2027-28 trough.
Capital allocation is set by COSCO Shipping (~75%): further newbuild orders or related-party arrangements could consume net cash that this model credits to minorities.
LBCT minimum-lift deficiency payments could exceed the US$877m provision if US import volumes stay weak.
Fuel and carbon costs (EU ETS at 100% from 2026, IMO net-zero framework) may not be fully passed through.
The US$5.8bn cash is assumed fully available to equity; it also funds the business through the trough, so a deeper or longer bear cycle reduces it further than modelled.

inputs.share_count_basis: 660,373,297 ordinary shares in issue at 30-Jun-2026 (share capital US$66.0m, unchanged since FY2022 scrip issues); no options or share awards outstanding, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: no SBC, no buyback, no announced issuance.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 bank interest income US$315.6m (Annual FY2025 note 7, line 7614) sits inside operating profit ('Others' in Container Transport) and therefore inside reported EBITDA, but the cash 'Interest received' (US$325.1m) is classified in INVESTING activities, so reported FCF (OCF - capex) already excludes it. The deduction in last_fcf is therefore 0 to avoid stripping it twice; the EBITDA margin paths below are built EX interest income (FY2025: 2,529.6 - 315.6 - 2.3 - 2.6 = 2,209 = 22.7% of revenue).
inputs.owner_fcf_after_leases_note: Under lease treatment (B) the comparable FY2025 owner FCF is reported FCF -35.1 less lease principal 656.1 = -691.2 (lease interest already inside OCF). Negative because FY2025 capex of US$2,026m was mostly newbuild instalments (7x24k TEU, 14x18.5k TEU programmes).
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment scheme; SBC is nil in FY2024-H1 2026 (US$0.1-4.8m in FY2019-2023, immaterial). Hong Kong SBC-zero filer.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in US$'000 (US$ functional currency); HKEX quote is HKD. Model values computed in USD and converted at USD/HKD 7.8472 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-10 21:00Z). Parity check: the H1-2026 interim dividend of US$0.55 is payable as HK$4.29 (company election rate 7.80, set 27-Aug-2026), within 0.6% of the market rate and the HKD peg band 7.75-7.85; direction confirmed (HKD per USD).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (HKEX 16:08 HKT); 52-week range 117.9-178.9. Price is ex the US$0.55 interim dividend (record date 18-Sep-2026).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.0 x 4.7% ERP = ~9.0%. Zero financial debt (leases are handled as an operating cost under treatment B), so WACC = cost of equity. Cyclicality and COSCO governance risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not as a WACC premium; the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (FY2025 principal 656.1 + lease interest ~18.3 = 674.4, 6.9% of revenue) is charged through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (US$1,272.1m at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is PPE + intangibles depreciation only, EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: 526.6 PPE vs 464.3 ROU). The six 13,000 TEU Seaspan 15-year charters (four delivering 2H 2026, two in 1Q 2028) lift the lease line in 2027-2028; the owned newbuild programme then replaces expiring charters, so the lease line glides down from 2030.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is US$5.1m of US$13,871m equity (0.04%); flows are whole-group and the NCI book value is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.capex_commitment_note: Contracted-but-not-provided vessel capex US$5,434.9m at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 note 20): remaining 6x24,168 TEU (delivering 4Q26-1Q28), 14x18,500 TEU methanol dual-fuel (3Q28-3Q29), 12x13,600 TEU LNG dual-fuel ordered H1-2026 (3Q28-1Q30). capex_pct_path carries these instalments as dollars (~US$1.5-1.7bn/yr 2026-2029 incl. ~US$250m/yr containers and other) and only then reverts to replacement capex.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the cyclical, non-US, lease, SBC-zero and dual-currency adaptations (owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Routing: OOIL is an operating company (container liner OOCL, >99% of revenue; Wall Street Plaza is <1%), not a financial, REIT or holdco, so owner-FCF applies; first valuation of this ticker, no prior model to match. MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: FY2021-22 (EBITDA 47-55% of revenue) are excluded as COVID supercycle; the margin anchor is the post-COVID / Red Sea era ex interest income (FY2023 21.1%, FY2024 29.3%, FY2025 22.7%, H1 2026 21.8%) cross-checked against the pre-COVID IFRS-16-equivalent ~16-18% (FY2018 NPAT US$108m on US$6.6bn revenue). Base mid-cycle EBITDA 19% sits between the two eras because the 2023-26 window was flattered by Red Sea diversions absorbing ~10% of global capacity, while the industry is structurally more consolidated than 2012-2019. The 2027-2028 trough reflects the record orderbook delivering into a Red Sea reopening. BRIDGE: cash and bank balances US$5,783.1m (includes deposits >3 months; no bank borrowings) plus the equity_bridge items (financial investments, Wall Street Plaza, JV/associates, LBCT onerous provision, declared interim dividend, NCI). Interest on the cash pile is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null. Buybacks: none; flat share count is not a funded policy, it simply reflects no issuance.

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: IFRS-16 EBITDA ex interest income. FY2026 ~20% (H1 21.8%; H2 weaker as the early peak season, oil spike and EU ETS cost bite). 2027-28 trough of 15-15.5% as the record orderbook delivers and Red Sea transits resume; recovery to a 19% mid-cycle by 2030.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 = H1 actual 830 + ~900 H2 instalments; 2027-2029 carry the US$5.4bn contracted vessel commitments plus ~US$250m/yr containers; from 2031 replacement capex ~8% of revenue against owned-fleet depreciation ~7.3% (fleet ~US$14bn gross over 25 years plus containers).
base.cash_tax_rationale: Shipping income largely under tonnage/exempt regimes: cash tax paid US$34m on PBT US$1,530m in FY2025 (2.2%), US$27m on US$2,614m in FY2024. 3% allows for minimum-tax creep; international shipping is excluded from Pillar Two GloBE income.
base.wc_rationale: Creditors and accruals (US$1.89bn) exceed debtors plus inventories (US$1.22bn), so revenue growth releases a little cash; 5% of the revenue change, symmetric on the way down.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default because the record orderbook, the Red Sea reopening and OOIL's own fixed US$5.4bn newbuild commitment are known, dated supply events rather than hypothetical risks, and the industry's history (2012-2019) is one of overcapacity. Base 50% as the central normalisation path. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once - continued Suez closure, orderbook absorption via scrapping/slow-steaming, and margin discipline among nine carriers - none of which OOIL controls.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
